name: claude-permission-popup
description: Alerts you in VS Code when Claude Code is waiting for permission approval

untrustedWorkspaces.description: This extension runs an HTTP server and requires a trusted workspace.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run lint && npm run test

claudePermissionPopup.port.description: Port for the notification HTTP server. Set to 0 (default) for a random available port. The actual port is written to a runtime file for the hook script to discover automatically.

claudePermissionPopup.osNotifications.description: Send OS-level notifications (via notify-send on Linux, osascript on macOS) when Claude Code is waiting for permission. Useful when VS Code is not in the foreground.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Claude Permission Popup
walkthroughs.description: Set up the Claude Code permission popup in a few steps.

steps.title: Verify Extension Activation
steps.description:
The extension starts automatically. Look for the shield icon in the status bar: **$(shield) Claude Permissions**.

Click it to open the extension logs.

media.markdown: The status bar should show **$(shield) Claude Permissions** when the extension is active.

steps.title: Install the Hook Script
steps.description:
Run the **Claude Permission Popup: Install Hook** command from the Command Palette to automatically configure the hook in your `.claude/settings.json`.

[Install Hook](command:claudePermissionPopup.installHook)

media.markdown: This writes the hook configuration so Claude Code notifies the extension when permission is needed.

steps.title: Test the Integration
steps.description:
Start Claude Code and trigger any tool that requires permission (e.g., a Bash command). You should see a VS Code warning notification, a yellow status bar, and an OS notification.

Approve or deny the request in the terminal.

Check the **Output** panel → **Claude Permission Popup** for logs.

media.markdown: You should see a warning notification with a **Show Terminal** button and the status bar turning yellow.
